mappings.note: A fruit seller taking QR-code payments straight into his account identified as digital money. Modern market practice under the goal; not LO-229, because no field enquiry into a market is asked.
The RBI's sole authority over currency and why central control keeps the system stable. The role of a government institution in the economy, which the goal names.
Matches forms of money to their eras and traits, with one wrong pairing. The evolution of money as an institution, so the goal.
Rejects the claim that digital money needs physical presence. Modern payment practice under the goal.
The Aztec tajadero shaped like an axe head. Another example of commodity money under the goal.
Matches the functions of money to their descriptions. Core economic concepts under the goal.
Money as a store of value because, unlike perishables, it keeps. A function of money under the goal.
Finds the item wrongly listed as early commodity money. Economic history of exchange under the goal.
The keyed statement is that money gives a common measure of value. A function of money under the goal.
Students swapping books recognised as barter. Economic concept applied to everyday life, so the goal.
Sorts real barter problems from a non-problem. Economic reasoning under the goal.
Dates the beginning of metal coinage in India. A chronological fact about the past, so the history goal rather than the economics one.
Defines commodities in the economic sense. Economic vocabulary under the goal.

Sets a single national issuer of paper currency against rulers who each minted their own coins. The modern half is an institution of the economy (CG-SST4), the earlier half is historical coinage (CG-SST2).
What the two stripes in the rupee symbol stand for. A fact about the national currency, so the goal.
Trading old clothes for new utensils recognised as surviving barter. Economic concept in daily life, so the goal.
Paying for a bicycle in instalments illustrates money as a standard of deferred payment. A function of money under the goal.
Finds the false statement about ancient Indian coinage. Historical coins as evidence, so CG-SST2.
Each new form of money answering a limitation of the last. A judgement about the evolution of a market institution, so the goal.
The keyed statement is money as a common unit of account. A function of money under the goal.
Names the missing double coincidence of wants. Economic reasoning under the goal.
Defines currency for a country's economy. Economic vocabulary under the goal.
Security features on notes as a guard against counterfeiting. The state's role in protecting the currency, so the goal.
Barter surviving at the Junbeel Mela alongside modern money read as older and newer systems coexisting. Economic institutions under the goal; LO-229 is reserved for field enquiries into a market.
Why alloy coins suit everyday use better than pure gold or silver. Economic reasoning about the form of money.
Picks the correctly defined money term. Economic vocabulary under the goal.
A government issuing commemorative legal tender falls under its control of coinage and currency. The role of government in the economy, which the goal names.
Sorts the primary functions of money from a non-function. Core economic concepts under the goal.
Matching set over currency, alloy and related terms. Economic vocabulary under the goal.
Names barter as direct exchange without money. The chapter's founding concept under the goal.
Names a commodity once used as money. Economic history of exchange under the goal.
Names the rai stones of Yap. Another commodity-money example under the goal.
Names the double coincidence of wants. Economic concept under the goal.
Names the divisibility problem in barter. Economic reasoning under the goal.
Names the portability problem in barter. Same lane as the other barter-limitation items.
Names the durability problem in barter. Economic reasoning under the goal.
Money as the invention that overcame barter's limits. The chapter's central economic development.
Money's function as a medium of exchange. A function of money under the goal.
Money as a store of value. A function of money under the goal.
A duplicate of the store-of-value question, with a stray fragment about portability appended. Same function-of-money content, so the same code.
